questions.prompt: Who executes a hook's command when its event fires?

options.text: Claude decides whether to run it, like any instruction
The Claude Code harness runs it automatically — the model has no say
You are prompted to run it manually

questions.explanation: That's the whole point: hooks are deterministic automation. A CLAUDE.md instruction is followed with high probability; a hook fires with certainty, every matching event.

questions.prompt: You want the test suite to run automatically after Claude edits any file. Which hook event and matcher?
questions.explanation: PostToolUse fires after a tool completes; the Edit|Write matcher scopes it to file modifications. PreToolUse would run tests before the edit — pointless here.

questions.prompt: Which task is a hook the WRONG choice for?

options.text: Deciding whether a code change also needs a documentation update
Playing a sound when Claude finishes

questions.explanation: Hooks are dumb and deterministic — perfect for always-do-X, wrong for judgment calls. 'Does this need a doc update?' requires understanding the change: that's an instruction for the model.

questions.prompt: Which are true about hook safety? (select all that apply)

options.text: Hooks run arbitrary shell commands with your user's permissions
You should review hooks configured in a repository you just cloned
Hooks can only run read-only commands
A PreToolUse hook can block a dangerous tool call before it happens

questions.explanation: Hooks are real shell commands — powerful for guardrails (d) and equally powerful for mischief, so audit configs you didn't write. Nothing restricts them to read-only.
